newsitem.title: USA: American Interactive to unveil Internet TV.
newsitem.headline: American Interactive to unveil Internet TV.

text.p: American Interactive Media on Friday said it expects to unveil in August its set-top box that will give a regular television access to the Internet.

The company said it has lined up content providers for its WebPASSPORT System, including several national newpapers, popular magazines and cable TV channels. The providers will have "channels" which will be carried on the WebPASSPORT system.
American Interactive said it will not charge for the device itself. Instead it will give customers the set-top unit when they sign up for service, which will probably cost about $30 per month.
It had previously said the device would sell for under $400.
The company's internet TV product will compete with Microsoft Corp's WebTV and Curtis Mathes Holding Corp's Internet TV set-top boxes.
